mainTopic: How long someone must use a property to gain a חזקה, the מחלוקת about a rain-watered field, and the גמרא's source for the three years in שור המועד.
overview: This new פרק opens with a משנה listing properties that give profit all year round, like houses, pits, bathhouses and slaves. For these, a חזקה is set after three full years of use, counted from day to day. A field watered only by rain gives profit only in certain seasons, so its three years are not counted day by day. רבי ישמעאל says eighteen months spread over three years are enough, and רבי עקיבא says fourteen months are enough. רבי ישמעאל adds that in a field of trees, three harvests of different crops count as three years. The גמרא then asks where the three years come from. רבי יוחנן reports that it is learned from שור המועד, an ox whose status changes after three gorings. The גמרא challenges this: the owner of such an ox pays full damages only from the fourth goring, so maybe a חזקה should need four years. It begins to answer that the ox's status already changes after three gorings, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Properties that produce all year need three full years
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists properties that constantly give profit and rules that their חזקה takes three full years, counted day by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: For houses, pits, ditches, caves, dovecotes, bathhouses, olive presses, irrigated fields, slaves, and anything that always produces profit, the חזקה is three years, counted from day to day.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the new פרק by setting the basic rule. Property that gives profit all year round needs three full years of use, counted from a given day to the same day three years later, to create a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person holding someone else's property can be presumed the owner if he used it openly for three years. For property that can be used every day, "three years" means exactly three years, from a given date to the same date three years later. The phrase "anything that always produces profit" tells us the list is only examples of a wider category.

keyTerms.meaning: Presumed ownership, created by using a property openly over time
An irrigated field that people water by hand or by channels
Dovecotes, places where pigeons are raised
Constant profits, produced all year round
From day to day, meaning full, exact years

steps.confusionAlert: Three years of use does not "buy" the property by itself. The חזקה is a strong presumption that the holder really did buy or receive it, since a real owner would have protested within that time.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the standard three-year rule that the rest of the פרק builds on.

phrases.english: The presumptive ownership of houses, and pits, and ditches,
and caves, and dovecotes, and bathhouses,
and olive presses, and irrigated fields,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָעֲבָדִים, וְכׇל שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה פֵּירוֹת תָּדִיר –
phrases.english: and slaves, and anything that constantly produces profits –
their presumptive ownership is three years, from day to day.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Property that produces profit all year needs three full years of use, counted day by day, to establish a חזקה.

steps.title: A rain-watered field needs three years, but not full ones
steps.stepSummary: A field watered only by rain also needs three years, but they are not counted day by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a rain-watered field, the חזקה is three years, but they do not need to be full years from day to day.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second rule for a field that only produces in certain seasons. It still needs three years, but not three exact calendar years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rain-watered field is not worked or harvested all year. So it is enough to use it during three growing seasons, even if the total time is less than three full years. This is the same three-year category, applied differently because of how the field is used.

keyTerms.meaning: A field watered only by rain

phrases.english: A rain-watered field – its presumptive ownership is three years,
but they are not from day to day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 1: same three years, but counted differently for a seasonal field.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rain-watered field needs three years of use, but they need not be full years counted day by day.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: eighteen months are enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל explains that three months in the first year, twelve in the middle, and three in the last count as three years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: three months in the first year, three in the last year, and twelve months in the middle. That is eighteen months.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל explains how short the first and last years can be for a rain-watered field. Eighteen months spread over three years are enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle year must be complete. The first and last years each need only three months of use, enough for a harvest season. So the field is used in three separate years, even though the total is only eighteen months.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says: Three months in the first year,
three months in the last year,
and twelve months in the middle;
that makes eighteen months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines how much time the "not day by day" years of step 2 must contain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a rain-watered field, three months in the first year, twelve in the middle, and three in the last (eighteen months) establish a חזקה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: fourteen months are enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that only one month in the first and last years is needed, for a total of fourteen months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: one month in the first year, one month in the last year, and twelve months in the middle. That is fourteen months.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי ישמעאל and requires even less time in the first and last years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the middle year must be complete. They argue only about the edge years: רבי ישמעאל needs three months in each, while רבי עקיבא needs just one month. So for רבי עקיבא, fourteen months spread over three years are enough.
steps.whatToRemember: Year-round property needs three full years for a חזקה. A rain-watered field needs use in three separate years: a full middle year, plus three months (רבי ישמעאל) or one month (רבי עקיבא) in each of the first and last years.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: A month in the first year,
and a month in the last year,
and twelve months in the middle;
that makes fourteen months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing opinion to רבי ישמעאל in step 3 on the same question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a rain-watered field, one month in the first year, twelve in the middle, and one in the last (fourteen months) establish a חזקה.

steps.title: In a field of trees, three harvests count as three years
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל limits the eighteen-month rule to a grain field. In a field of trees, harvesting grain, olives and figs counts as three years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said: When does this rule apply? In a grain field. But in a field of trees, if he gathered his grain, harvested his olives and gathered his figs, these count as three years.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל adds one more case to his earlier rule. A field of trees works differently from a plain grain field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי ישמעאל said a rain-watered field needs about eighteen months spread over three years. Here he says that rule is only for a שדה לבן, a field with just one crop. In a שדה אילן, three separate harvests of three different crops act like three 'years' of use, even if they all happen within a short time.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'white field': an open grain field with no trees

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי ישמעאל, three harvests of different crops in a field of trees count as three years of חזקה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said:
In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: He means the eighteen-month rule from step 3.

phrases.english: In a white field,
phrases.notes: A 'white field' is an open grain field with no trees shading it.

phrases.english: but in a field of trees,
if he gathered his grain,
and harvested his olives,
and gathered his summer fruit,
these count as three years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי ישמעאל's position from step 3 by limiting it to a grain field and adding a special rule for a field of trees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a field of trees, three harvests of different crops count as three years for חזקה.

steps.title: The three-year rule is learned from the forewarned ox
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that he heard from those who traveled to אושא that the three years of חזקה are learned from שור המועד, which changes status after three gorings.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי יוחנן said: I heard from those who traveled to אושא that they would say: How do we know that חזקה takes three years? From the forewarned ox. After a forewarned ox gores three times, it leaves the status of an innocent ox and gets the status of a forewarned ox. Here too, once he has used the land for three years, it leaves the seller's ownership and is held to be in the buyer's ownership.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks where the number three comes from. It answers with a comparison to an ox that gored three times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox starts out as a תם, an 'innocent' ox. After three gorings it becomes a מועד, a 'forewarned' ox. The scholars say land works the same way: three years of use shift the land from the seller's ownership to the buyer's. In both cases, three repeated events create a new presumed status.

keyTerms.meaning: A forewarned ox: one that has gored three times, so its owner pays full damages
An 'innocent' ox with no record of goring; its owner pays only half damages
A town in the גליל where the חכמים had their center

steps.confusionAlert: This is a logical comparison, not a derivation from a פסוק. The scholars are only learning the number three from the ox. The other details of the ox laws do not automatically carry over, which is exactly what the next step tests.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the גמרא's first attempt to find a source for the three years of חזקה. The challenge that follows will test how far the comparison goes.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rabbi Yochanan said:
I heard from those who travel to Usha
that they would say:
From where do we know that presumptive ownership takes three years?
From the forewarned ox.
Just as with a forewarned ox,
once it has gored three times,
it leaves the status of an innocent ox,
and takes on the status of a forewarned ox;
here too,
once he has used it for three years,
it leaves the seller's ownership,
and is held to be in the buyer's ownership.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by looking for the source of the three-year rule taught in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three years of חזקה are learned from שור המועד, which becomes forewarned after three gorings.

steps.title: Then the buyer should need a fourth year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the ox comparison further. The owner pays full damages only from the fourth goring, so maybe the land should belong to the buyer only from the fourth year.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then just as with a forewarned ox the owner is not liable for full damages until the fourth goring, here too the land should not be held in the buyer's ownership until the fourth year!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison to the ox. It points out a detail of the ox laws that would lead to a different number of years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Full payment for a forewarned ox only starts with the fourth goring. If חזקה really copies the ox, ownership should only take effect in the fourth year. That would contradict the three years taught in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge built on what was just said)

phrases.english: If so,
just as with a forewarned ox,
the owner is not liable until the fourth goring,
phrases.notes: He means liable for full damages. Before that, the owner pays only half.

phrases.english: here too,
until the fourth year
it should not be held in his ownership!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה שׁוֹר הַמּוּעָד עַד נְגִיחָה רְבִיעִית לָא מִיחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ox comparison from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of חזקה to שור המועד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If חזקה follows the ox, it should also follow the ox's fourth-goring liability. That would mean four years, not three.

steps.title: The comparison holds: the ox's status changes after three gorings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. The ox's status already changes after the third goring, and that change of status is the point being compared.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, once it has gored three times, it is already forewarned,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the challenge by showing the two cases are not really parallel the way the question assumed. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ox's new status is set right after the third goring. Liability only appears at the fourth goring because that is the first time the now-forewarned ox causes damage. What we compare to חזקה is the change of status after three, not the timing of payment. The rest of the answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (a phrase that rejects a comparison)

phrases.english: How can you compare these?!
There, once it has gored three times,
it is already forewarned,
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished here. The answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7 and defends the comparison from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing what is actually being compared (status versus payment)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ox comparison would require four years, since full liability starts only at the fourth goring.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ox becomes forewarned right after three gorings. That change of status is what parallels three years of חזקה.
